I read both steps, the signature of `regDirichletIntegral_tangent_ibp`, and `ContDiffNearStdSimplex` and its API in StdSimplexMeasure/Smooth.lean. findings.problem: The inductive step repeats the real-kernel proof in Transform.lean almost line for line. The repeated parts are: (1) the real-part bounds `hshift` and `hshift'`, which show `l.length + 2 < Re` after shifting by `e_j` and by `e_j - e_i`, a case split on `k = j` and `k = i` with `simp`/`linarith`; (2) the extraction of `DifferentiableAt` from `ContDiffNearStdSimplex`, namely `obtain ⟨V,hV,hsub,hfV⟩ … hfV.contDiffAt (hV.mem_nhds (hsub hu))).differentiableAt (by simp)`; and (3) the integration-by-parts step, namely `regDirichletIntegral_tangent_ibp` with the `2 ≤ l.length + 2` side condition, then `add_sub_cancel_right`, then `change … fderiv ℝ …`, then `rw`, then `ring`. The two theorems differ only in how the kernel is presented. A fix to the bound arithmetic or the IBP bookkeeping has to be made in both places, and the real version is private, so the target cannot reuse it.
findings.proposed_change: Extract three public lemmas in Transform.lean (or Smooth.lean) and use them in both theorems. (a) `ContDiffNearStdSimplex.differentiableAt (hf : ContDiffNearStdSimplex (N+1) f) : ∀ u ∈ coordinateSet ℝ ι, DifferentiableAt ℝ f u`. The proof is the existing `obtain` block. (b) `shift_re_lt (i) (j : {j // j ≠ i}) (n : ℕ) {b : ι → ℂ} (hb : ∀ k, (n:ℝ) + 1 + 2 < (b k).re) : (∀ k, (n:ℝ)+2 < ((b + Pi.single j 1) k).re) ∧ (∀ k, (n:ℝ)+2 < ((b + Pi.single j 1 - Pi.single i 1) k).re)`. The proof is the existing `hshift`/`hshift'` arguments. (c) `regDirichletIntegral_shift_step (i) (j) (n) {b} (hb : ∀ k, (n:ℝ)+2 < ((b + Pi.single j 1) k).re) {f} (hdiff : ∀ u ∈ coordinateSet ℝ ι, DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (hcont : ContinuousOn (fun u => fderiv ℝ f u (Pi.single j 1 - Pi.single i 1)) (coordinateSet ℝ ι)) : regDirichletIntegral (b + Pi.single j 1 - Pi.single i 1) f - regDirichletIntegral (b + Pi.single j 1) (fun u => fderiv ℝ f u (Pi.single j 1 - Pi.single i 1)) = regDirichletIntegral b f`. The proof is the current `hIBP`, `add_sub_cancel_right`, `ring` block. In `shiftedDirichletIntegral_eq`, the cons case becomes `obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := shift_re_lt i j l.length hb; rw [shiftedDirichletIntegral, ih _ h2, ih hdf h1]; exact regDirichletIntegral_shift_step i j _ h1 hf'.differentiableAt hdf.continuousOn`. In the target, the cons case becomes `obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := shift_re_lt i j l.length hb; rw [shiftedComplexKernelIntegral, ih hH h2, ih (analyticOnNhd_complexSimplexTangentDeriv hH j i) h1, regDirichletIntegral_congr _ (fun u hu => complexSimplexTangentDeriv_eq_real hH z (hW u hu) j i)]; exact regDirichletIntegral_shift_step i j _ h1 hf.differentiableAt (hf.tangentDeriv j i).continuousOn`, with `hf := contDiffNearStdSimplex_complexKernel hWo hH z hW 1` as already in the file. Only the congruence by `complexSimplexTangentDeriv_eq_real` remains specific to the complex kernel. The `change` that unfolds `stdSimplexTangentDeriv` to `fderiv … (Pi.single j 1 - Pi.single i 1)` may still be needed.
findings.benefit: The roughly 40-line IBP/bounds argument is proved once. Each shifted-equality theorem shrinks to its kernel-specific rewrites. The `l.length + 2` threshold and the form of the IBP step are fixed in one place. The `hdiff` extraction also becomes reusable API.
